findings.finding: The doc admits the SBOM version sort "loses its optional `packaging` import under the isolated env and falls back to a cruder sort." This is not an uncovered pre-existing gap (like the bash hooks) — it is a behavior regression caused by this change: previously `packaging` was picked up from the ambient environment, and the new header cuts that off. The spec claims "Spec Impact: NONE," so accepting a silently degraded sort contradicts that claim, and it's fixed trivially.
findings.suggestion: Add `"packaging"` to the header's `dependencies` for `audit_compliance_on_stop.py` (and mirror it in `--with` if you want the codex-bundle dedup shape unchanged — the superset test tolerates extra header deps). Remove the "falls back to a cruder sort" sentence.  2. Category: test | Severity: medium

findings.finding: The ledger regex only matches `uv run <flags> "quoted-target"` — a hooks.json entry written as `uv run --no-project ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/.../hook.py` (unquoted), `uv run ... python script.py`, or using `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` without braces is silently dropped from `_entry_points()`, so a new headerless hook of that shape would pass CI. The `>= 30` floor only detects catastrophic regex breakage, not single-entry drift, and `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` handling is additionally hardcoded to the braced form (an unbraced path resolves to a nonexistent file and fails at collection, not as a clean test failure).
findings.suggestion: Also parse the unquoted form (e.g. fall back to splitting the command and taking the first token ending in `.py` after `uv run`), and make path resolution assert on unresolved variables rather than silently producing a bad Path.  3. Category: test | Severity: low

findings.finding: Module-level `assert len(_ENTRY_POINTS) >= 30` and the `_PROBED` name assertion turn fixture drift into collection errors for the whole module — all tests report as errors, and on some CI setups a collection error in one file can obscure results in others. Also the doc claims "empty stderr" was verified, but the test only asserts `"error:" not in proc.stderr`, which is weaker than the documented claim (a hook emitting noise on stderr would pass).
findings.suggestion: Move both into real tests (or a session-scoped fixture raising `pytest.fail`), and assert `proc.stderr.strip() == ""` if the empty-stderr claim is meant to be load-bearing.  4. Category: test | Severity: low

findings.finding: The poisoned-CWD behavioral test probes only 2 of ~35 entry points (`suggest_iterate.py`, `audit_compliance_on_stop.py`). Static header-shape tests cover all 35, but a malformed-but-parseable header on any of the other 33 (e.g. a dependency typo like `yaml` instead of `pyyaml` that still parses as a name) is only caught by the `--with` superset test, not by an actual run. This matches the review record's deliberate probe cut, so it's a calibration note, not a blocker.
findings.suggestion: Optionally rotate one more `pyyaml`-dependent entry point into `_PROBED_NAMES`, or leave as-is given the documented concurrency cost.  5. Category: bug | Severity: low

findings.finding: _hook_commands` glob is `plugins//hooks/hooks.json` — it matches any `hooks.json` (e.g. a `hooks.dev.json` or `hooks.codex.json` if one exists), and the resolve-relative-to-plugin-root assumption (`hooks_path.parent.parent`) only holds if hooks.json sits exactly two levels below the plugin root. If the codex bundle sync produces a differently-nested hooks file, the ledger's path resolution silently produces wrong Paths. Low because the current tree presumably matches.
findings.suggestion: Assert the resolved path exists before use so drift fails loudly instead of producing `FileNotFoundError` at parametrize time.  Spec compliance check: AC-1 through AC-7 are all implemented. AC-6 is verifiable from the diff: all 12 vendored `run_if_cache_ready.py` copies plus the template share the same before/after blob hashes, so they remain byte-identical. AC-5's rewrite of the #814 negative control to a headerless probe is done as described. The `--no-project` layer is asserted twice (old test file and new `test_no_project_still_present_alongside_headers`). No security issues found.  Overall: ship-with-fixes — the approach is sound and well-tested, but the `packaging` regression in `audit_compliance_on_stop` should be fixed rather than documented, and the ledger regex's unquoted-command blind spot slightly undermines the "a new hook without a header fails CI" guarantee.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.file: shared/tests/test_hooks_pep723_isolation.py:36` — Finding: The hook ledger recognizes only `uv run` targets in double quotes. A new command such as `uv run --no-project ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/hooks/new.py` would be omitted, so it could lack a PEP 723 header while the tests still pass. This breaks AC-3’s requirement that a new headerless hook fail CI.
findings.finding: Parse every `uv run` command shape accepted in `hooks.json`, and fail explicitly when a command cannot be mapped to a script.
